label: build:audio
mission: All sounds synthesized with WebAudio: AudioWorklet V8 engine (firing-frequency synthesis, exhaust resonances, on/off-throttle character, limiter), turbo and blow-off, opponents, tire screech, wind and rain, impacts, scrapes, UI, procedural synthwave music; verified analytically with OfflineAudioContext.

structured_report.summary:
I built the complete procedural audio system for section 9. It uses no audio files, every public method is a safe no-op before `init()` or without WebAudio, and it was verified offline and in a real-time context. It already matches how core calls it (`src/core/audiomix.js`, `game.js`).

**Player engine** (AudioWorklet in `engineWorklet.js`, loaded from a Blob URL):
- **Firing model:** a 4-stroke cycle at rpm/120 Hz with 8 firings per cycle in a crossplane V8 order. Each bank sees uneven firing intervals, which produces the real V8 half-order burble. Each cylinder has a fixed amplitude/timing bias, and each firing gets random amplitude and timing jitter, plus off-throttle dropouts.
- **Pulse shape:** each firing is a fractionally placed (band-limited) impulse into a bi-exponential pressure-pulse shaper. The pulse has a steep blowdown edge and a decay that scales with crank angle, and it gets sharper under load.
- **Resonances:** each bank feeds its own exhaust pipe (feedback comb with in-loop damping; length tracks gas temperature), then a muffler chamber. These resonances stay fixed while the harmonics sweep through them, which gives the howl.
- **Other layers:** an intake pipe with induction roar, combustion noise modulated by the pulses, valvetrain ticks, a micro rpm wander, and an asymmetric soft-clip for growl. A 30 Hz high-pass removes sub-audio, and a morphing output EQ blends the two characters: bright and loud on throttle, muffled and boomy on overrun.
- **Events:** an idle-fueling model keeps bark at idle. Overrun crackles are self-generated after a lift, and their crack bypasses the muffled EQ. The rev limiter stutters with a fuel cut at about 14 Hz. Upshifts get a 75 ms ignition cut that gates firings, so it can't click.
- All controls are AudioParams driven with `setTargetAtTime`, plus per-sample smoothing inside the worklet.

**Other layers (native nodes):**
- **Turbo:** a lagged spool model with a whistle (two partials plus a narrow noise band). There is a blow-off valve hiss with compressor-surge flutter on loaded upshifts and on lift-off.
- **Opponents:** a second worklet with 4 cheap V8/flat-6/V10 voices, equal-power pan, distance attenuation and air-absorption low-pass. Doppler is estimated from the rate of change of distance, and there is a pass-by whoosh when a rival is close. A second output feeds the reverb with gentler (square-root) attenuation, so distant cars sound more reverberant.
- **Tires and environment:**
  - Tire screech: two high-Q squeal bands with LFO and random-walk wobble, plus a wet tread hiss (dominant by default, wet = 0.85) and scrub rumble.
  - Wind, road roar and wet spray hiss all rise with speed, plus rain hitting the car.
  - Ambience: a decorrelated stereo rain bed, puddle droplets, distant city rumble, occasional thunder and a rare distant siren.
- **Nitro:** a hiss/air/rumble loop with flutter, an activation whoosh and a release psst; it also makes the engine more aggressive.
- **One-shots:**
  - Impact: thump, distorted crunch, crumple, scattered metal pings, and glass tinkle on hard hits.
  - Scrape: continuous calls are fine; stick-slip grit modulation, metal ring bands, rate-limited updates and auto-release about 90 ms after the last call.
  - Backfire: 1–3 pops (crack plus thump, big reverb send) that also trigger engine crackles.
  - Shift clunk: a downshift on overrun can add a crackle.
  - Countdown beeps (G5, then G6 for GO), UI hover/select, lap stinger and finish stinger.
- **Reverb:** a convolver with a procedurally generated 1.4 s street-canyon impulse response (façade slap-back reflections plus a darkening tail).
- **Music:** dark synthwave in A minor at 120 BPM with a look-ahead scheduler (25 ms timer plus pumping from `update`). Kick, a gated-reverb snare, 16th hats, an octave-bouncing saw bass, a detuned saw pad with sidechain pump, and an arp with a dotted-8th delay. It follows a 64 s song form (A / B with arp / breakdown / build with snare roll / B2 with crash cymbals), so it doesn't loop a short pattern.
- **Master chain:** glue compressor → limiter → master gain (volume/mute) → transparent safety soft-clipper.
- **Robustness:**
  - A watchdog fades the car layers if `setEngine` stops arriving.
  - The context suspends while the tab is hidden.
  - A gesture listener resumes the context if `init()` wasn't called inside a gesture.
  - If AudioWorklet is unavailable (e.g. plain http on a LAN IP), a native oscillator engine takes over.

**Verification** (`dev/audio.html`): an interactive bench (sliders, auto rpm sweep, simulated drivetrain on W/S/Space/Shift, every SFX button, opponents and fly-by, live analyser) and an automated offline analysis via `?autotest=<id>`.
- **Engine points:** the f_fire peak sits within 0.3% of rpm/60×4 at 900–8000 rpm, standing 23–47 dB above its neighbourhood. The magnitude-weighted spectral centroid rises monotonically at full throttle: 1715 → 2251 → 2631 → 2714 Hz for 3500–7800 rpm.
- **Levels:** idle −27 dB RMS, full throttle −13 to −17 dB RMS, overrun −24 to −31.
- **Peaks and validity:** the highest peak across all tests is −2.1 dBFS, with no NaN in any render and no silent output.
- **Drive run:** 13 s with shifts, lift-off and skid; the click detector finds none in the full mix. The only engine-only hit, at 9.37 s, is an intentional overrun crackle. At a 0→1 throttle step the max sample step is 0.008, versus 0.14 during steady full throttle.
- **Opponents:** fly-by doppler measured 458.8 / 355.5 Hz against 459.7 / 354 theoretical. Reversing the list order every 0.25 s keeps each voice on its car (31–40 dB channel separation).
- **Other checks:** the full race mix peaks at −2.9 dBFS (−16 RMS), and the robustness test reports zero throws. Spectrograms and waveforms are in `shots/audio-final-a.png`.
structured_report.contract_notes:
The required API is implemented with the exact names. All of the following are additive.

- **`createAudio(options)`** accepts optional:
  - `{ context, volume, muted }`;
  - `forceNative` (test only: skips the worklet).
- **`init()`** returns a Promise that resolves `true` when ready and `false` if WebAudio is unavailable. It is idempotent; repeat calls retry `resume()`.
- **Extra methods:** `setMuted(bool)` (core already uses it for `?mute=1`), `setPaused(bool)` (ducks car layers and one-shots, music to 60%; core already calls it), `setWet(0..1)`, `playBlowOff(strength)`, `playThunder()`, `playSiren()`.
- **Extra getters:** `muted`, `ready`, `context`, `engineKind` (`'worklet'` or `'native'`), plus test hooks `_graph` and `_pumpMusic`.
- **Interpretations:**
  - `pan`: +1 = right (matches core's camera-right projection).
  - `distance`: metres from the listener/camera.
  - The opponents list may arrive in any order; entries are matched to voices by continuity, and anything beyond 4 is ignored.
  - `load` defaults to `throttle` when omitted.
  - `gear < 0` adds a straight-cut reverse whine; `gear` and `speedKmh` otherwise only drive a faint drivetrain whine.
  - `setNitro(active)` is edge-triggered (whoosh on rising edge, psst on falling).
  - `playShift(up)` with throttle or load > 0.35 adds a 75 ms ignition cut, may add an exhaust crackle, and plays the blow-off/flutter when boost or load is high.
  - `toggleMute()` returns `true` when now muted. Mute, volume, ambience and music requests made before `init()` are stored and applied at init.
- **Behaviour to be aware of:**
  - The car layers (engine, opponents, tires, wind, scrape, nitro, and their reverb sends) stay silent until the first `setEngine` call. They fade out if `setEngine` stops for more than 450 ms; menus with no engine feed are therefore silent apart from ambience, music and UI.
  - The engine produces its own overrun crackles after high-rpm lifts (about 4.5 per second, decaying over about 2 s), in addition to core's `playBackfire()` calls. If the combination is too crackly, core can call `playBackfire` less often.
  - Core currently calls `setMusic(true)` at the menu unlock; the music plays at about −28 dB RMS, roughly 12 dB under a full-throttle engine.
known_issues: I can't listen, so timbre is verified only analytically (spectra, waveforms, spectrograms, levels). The final engine character (exhaust pipe lengths of 1.92 m and 2.31 m, the output EQ, and the MIX table at the top of `audio.js`) may need tuning by ear.

The power-weighted spectral centroid is not monotonic at 7800 rpm full throttle: the strong f_fire line and its half-order dominate the power weighting there. The magnitude-weighted centroid does rise monotonically.

In OfflineAudioContext renders, worklet port messages (opponent updates, `playBackfire` engine pops) are only delivered at suspend points. The bench uses suspend steps for this; real-time contexts are unaffected.

Vite full-reloads every page whenever `index.html` changes, which repeatedly interrupted long bench runs. The bench now checkpoints each stage in sessionStorage keyed by `?autotest=<id>`; use a new id for each fresh run.
The native fallback engine (no AudioWorklet, e.g. plain http on a non-localhost IP) is a simpler oscillator stack: it renders correctly but sounds much less realistic.
Visibility handling suspends the AudioContext while the tab is hidden and resumes it when visible. If core also manages suspension, the two could interact, though core doesn't today.
structured_report.perf_notes:
Main thread: the whole per-frame call set (`setEngine`, `setOpponents` with 4 rivals, `setSkid`, `setWind`, occasional `playScrape`, `update`) costs about 0.0115 ms per frame, measured over 3000 iterations. That is under 0.1% of a 16.7 ms frame.

Parameter pushes are change-thresholded so they don't flood the automation timeline. Opponent messages are throttled to about 33 Hz. One-shots build small node chains that disconnect themselves when they end, and the music creates roughly 100 short-lived nodes per second.

Audio rendering thread, measured offline on one core with the machine idle:
- Engine worklet: about 0.8–0.9% (it does per-32-sample coefficient updates).
- Opponents worklet: about 0.1%.
- Whole system with every layer active: about 7.8%, mostly the convolver and the native filter/noise layers. Later readings were much higher only because other agents' benches were loading the machine.

To keep native cost down, silent layers (skid, scrape, nitro, turbo noise, ambience) are gated at their source, so their filters receive silence and Chrome can skip them. The reverb impulse response was shortened to 1.4 s.

Init generates the noise, droplet and grit buffers in about 20–40 ms on the main thread; impulse-response generation is deferred one tick. There is no per-frame garbage beyond tiny arrays.
